paraphrase: Thesis of the Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣad, decided from the six marks of purport. The text identifies Oṃ, all time, brahman and the self (MU 1, 2, 8, 12) and teaches that this self has four quarters: waking (vaiśvānara), dream (taijasa) and deep sleep (prājña), which are matched to the measures a, u, m, and a fourth (caturtha) that is without measure and known only by negation and by the words "stilling of the world, auspicious, non-dual" (MU 7, 12). Opening and closing (upakrama-upasaṃhāra): the text begins with "Oṃ is all this" (MU 1) and ends with "Oṃ is just the self; one who knows thus enters the self by the self" (MU 12). Repetition (abhyāsa): the quarters/states and the phrase "ya evaṃ veda" are repeated for each measure (MU 9–11), and prapañcopaśama-śiva-advaita recurs at MU 7 and 12. Novelty (apūrvatā): the four-quarter scheme of the self, the fourth as the unspoken beyond the three states, and the quarter-measure correspondence are taught here without a stated earlier source in the text itself. Stated result (phala): obtaining all desires and becoming first (MU 9), raising the continuity of knowledge (MU 10), measuring all and becoming its merging (MU 11), and entering the self by the self (MU 12). Praise (arthavāda): the fruit-promises of MU 9–11 are in the form of praise of the knower; their weight is left to the interpretation layer. Reasoned demonstration (upapatti): the passages give brief grounds only for the a-u-m assignments (obtaining/being first; exaltation/both-ness; measuring/merging, MU 9–11); the four quarters are otherwise stated, not argued. Main teaching: the self is one and non-dual; the three states are its quarters and the fourth is its own nature; Oṃ, with its three measures and the measureless, is identified with this self and its quarters (MU 1, 8, 12).
speaker: Upaniṣad (śruti; no named speaker)
translation_basis: own summary made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Marks assessed by the extractor from the twelve sections; the weighting of the fruit-promises as arthavāda is not decided here.
